LanguageData.RC2_AsparagusBaseHydro.label: asparagus shoots
LanguageData.RC2_AsparagusBaseHydro.description: A short, fast-growing shoot whose young stalks are used as a vegetable. A versatile plant that grows anywhere but tropical regions.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantAgave.label: agave
LanguageData.RC2_PlantAgave.description: A large-leafed desert plant with edible flowers and stalks. This variant is better able to be tamed, although it can still only be grown in arid regions.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantAsparagus.label: asparagus shoots

LanguageData.RC2_PlantEggPlant.label: eggplant plant
LanguageData.RC2_PlantEggPlant.description: These spongy fruits are technically berries - but, use them like a berry, and you'll have a bad time. Instead, they're used similarly to vegetables. Grown in temperate and tropical climates.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantMushroom.label: common mushrooms
LanguageData.RC2_PlantMushroom.description: A small, white mushroom that has been cultivated for thousands of years. Does not require light to grow, but won't die when exposed to it. Variations exist to such an extent that they're found in every climate.

LanguageData.RC2_PlantPumpkin.label: pumpkin vine
LanguageData.RC2_PlantPumpkin.description: A vining plant that grows along the ground. It produces large, juicy pumpkins. Takes a while to grow. Does not react well to colder climates, but can be grown in temperate, tropical, and arid ones.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantSorghum.label: sorghum plants
LanguageData.RC2_PlantSorghum.description: A heat-loving grass with an edible grain. Very popular amongst desert-dwelling tribes and colonies, and takes fairly well to most soils.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantSugarcane.label: sugarcane reeds
LanguageData.RC2_PlantSugarcane.description: This tall grass has stalkes that, when processed, create a delicious sugar great for ruining your teeth. Also used for making rum! Why is the rum always gone? Only grown in tropical regions.
LanguageData.RC2_PlantTomato.label: tomato plant
LanguageData.RC2_PlantTomato.description: This bright red bulb is the fruit of a deadly strain of poisonous plants. The fruit itself is not poisonous, thankfully, and is actually quite delicious, especially when cooked into a sauce or made into ketchup. Although a fruit, the Toma Mato is classified as a vegetable by chefs. They don’t know any better. Likes temperate climates.

LanguageData.RC2_PlantYam.label: yam plant
LanguageData.RC2_PlantYam.description: This earthy tuber is similar to potato, but not. Some mistakenly use the name to refer to sweet potatoes (its not). Unlike its relative, the potato, yams only grow well in warm, wet climates.
